object_or_group: Kish, Mound A, Burial A51: the fifteen carnelian beads of one necklace, ED III, c.2600-2350 BCE
geological_source: Deccan Traps, India; within it, Gujarat at the regional level. Ten beads assign first to the Ratanpur deposit and four to Mardak Beyt, but see notes: the method's source-level resolution does not support naming a deposit.
analytical_provenance: LA-ICP-MS against a 25-source agate-carnelian reference database, evaluated by canonical discriminant analysis. Leave-one-out cross-validation 69.9% at source level, 93.9% at regional level (DRR-002).
workshop: Divided within one necklace. Eleven beads carry Indus finishing throughout. Four (1, 6, 13, 15) were drilled with Indus tools but finished to a different standard, which the study reads as finishing in Mesopotamia or manufacture there by Indus-trained hands (DRR-007).
manufacturing_tradition: Indus. All fifteen were perforated with constricted cylindrical Ernestite drills, a technology the study calls singularly distinctive of the Indus.
exporter: NOT ESTABLISHED - no text names a shipper of these beads and none is inferable from the objects.
intermediary: NOT ESTABLISHED - Dilmun and Magan are the candidates in the corridor literature; nothing in this object group evidences either.
textual_provenance_label: NOT ESTABLISHED for these objects. The Mesopotamian label usually attached to Indus goods is Meluhha, but no text is associated with this burial.
findspot: Kish (mod. Tell el-Uhaymir), Iraq, Mound A, Burial A51.
museum_attribution: Field Museum accession numbers of the form Kish 2285331 to 22853315 / 2885332 to 28853315 as printed in the study's figure captions; the two series differ between captions in the retrieved text and are recorded as printed rather than reconciled.
modern_custody: The Field Museum, Chicago, as of the study's 2025 acknowledgement of permission to study the beads.
open_licensed_image: NOT ACCESSIBLE - custodian databases refused at the egress gateway (SRC-099); D-055
locator: SRC-109 CARNELIAN BEADS FROM KISH chunks 6-7; EVALUATION OF THE RESULTS chunks 14-15; figure captions 2, 3 and 4
notes: The best-documented object group in this unit and the one that separates the most fields. PROVISIONAL not VERIFIED: the per-bead assignments live in supplementary appendices the passage-level lane did not deliver, and the analysis is not comparable with other laboratories (DRR-015), so it has no independent replication and cannot have one at present. Read the source assignment regionally: on the study's own cross-validation three geological samples in ten are misplaced at source level, and reducing the comparison to the ten Deccan sources did not improve it (DRR-003).

object_or_group: Kish, Burial A51: beads 1 and 15 of the same necklace, bleached carnelian with white designs
geological_source: As OBJ-R-001: Deccan Traps, Gujarat at regional resolution.
analytical_provenance: As OBJ-R-001; these two are not separated from the set by the geochemistry.
workshop: Not Indus, or not to Indus standard. Ends chipped and partly rounded rather than ground flat; the bleached designs executed with less refinement than beads 4 and 14 in the same necklace.
manufacturing_tradition: Indus in tooling - perforated with Indus-style constricted cylindrical drills - and non-Indus in finishing and decoration.
findspot: Kish, Mound A, Burial A51 (same necklace as OBJ-R-001).
museum_attribution: Field Museum; the bleached long barrel bead is figured as Kish 28853315 / 22853315.
open_licensed_image: NOT ACCESSIBLE - custodian databases refused at the egress gateway (SRC-099); D-055
locator: SRC-109 CARNELIAN BEADS FROM KISH chunk 6, and figure 4 captions c and d
notes: Given its own row because it is the case that breaks the fields apart hardest. Two beads on one string with the same geological source, the same drilling technology and a different workshop standard. Whether that means part-finishing in transit, a Mesopotamian workshop using Indus tools, or an Indus workshop working to a lower standard for export, the objects do not say, and the study offers the first two as alternatives. Any exhibit using this necklace should show the two beads beside beads 4 and 14, because the difference is visible and it is the argument.

notes: Recorded precisely because nothing is known about it. On one string, sixteen lapis beads travelled the Blue Road and fifteen carnelian beads travelled the Red Road, and only the second set has been analysed. The asymmetry is not about the objects; it reflects which specialists studied this necklace. The single most economical piece of new work this unit can name is the analysis of the lapis from this necklace against the same protocol, which would put both roads in one burial with one instrument.

intermediary: NOT ESTABLISHED - the study argues for an east-to-west route without evidencing a specific intermediary.

object_or_group: Ur, Royal Cemetery: etched and long biconical carnelian beads, ED III
geological_source: NOT ESTABLISHED - not analysed in any retrieved study.
analytical_provenance: NONE retrieved. The attribution to the Indus is stylistic and technological.
workshop: Contested since excavation. Woolley took the etched beads to be imported finished from the Indus while assuming other beads were made locally; Mackay held that the finely crafted carnelian beads were brought in. Later technological study of the Ur beads by the same methods as OBJ-R-001 concluded that many were made in Indus workshops and some, including long hexagonal shapes never produced in the Indus, were made locally with Indus technique.
manufacturing_tradition: Indus for the etched and long biconical types.
findspot: Ur (mod. Tell Muqayyar), Iraq, Royal Cemetery, c.2500-2450 BCE.
museum_attribution: Studied in the collections of the University of Pennsylvania Museum; no accession numbers in the retrieved passages.
modern_custody: Divided at excavation between the British Museum, the University of Pennsylvania Museum and Baghdad, on the standard partage of the Woolley expedition. This unit did not retrieve a custody list and does not assert one.
open_licensed_image: NOT ACCESSIBLE - custodian databases refused at the egress gateway (SRC-099); D-055
locator: SRC-109 INTRODUCTION AND BACKGROUND chunks 1 and 4, citing Woolley 1934: 206-207 and 372-373, Mackay 1929: 185, Kenoyer 1997 and 2008; SRC-120 BACKGROUND
notes: The most famous objects on the Red Road and, in this unit's evidence, the least analytically characterised: no geochemical provenance for the Ur beads was retrieved. Also the site of an early and instructive disagreement between two excavators, Woolley and Mackay, about workshop against import - the same question OBJ-R-001 answers with an instrument ninety years later. An unfinished-bead assemblage from Ur was noted by Woolley and, on SRC-109's account, never studied in detail.

object_or_group: Jebel al-Ma'taradh, Ra's al-Khaimah, UAE: the raw-material reference collection from twenty-six mapped veins
geological_source: The deposit itself: opaque and transparent carnelian, milky and brown chalcedony, agate, chrysoprase, black flint and chert, mapped vein by vein.
analytical_provenance: Not applicable - this is a source, not an artefact. Whether it is in any artefact-sourcing reference database is not established: the 25-source database at SRC-109 names Tayma and Sanaa among its Arabian entries, both proxies, and does not name Jebel al-Ma'taradh in any retrieved passage.
workshop: No bead workshop has been found at the deposit; the excavators expect them in settlements not yet discovered.
manufacturing_tradition: Neolithic lithic industries from the seventh millennium BC; bead production in these materials in the region is dated later.
textual_provenance_label: None. The region is conventionally identified as Magan, which is a label applied to it from Mesopotamia.
findspot: Jebel al-Ma'taradh and its surroundings, Emirate of Ra's al-Khaimah; material from it identified at Yahar, Falaj al-Mu'alla, Hamriah, Al Madar, Akab, Umm al-Quwain 2, Jezirat al-Hamra and, at 300 km, Marawah MR1.
museum_attribution: A reference collection, not accessioned objects.
modern_custody: Department of Antiquities of Ra's al-Khaimah, held at the disposal of researchers working in the UAE.

notes: Included as an object row although it is a source, because it is the entity the Red Road's alternative-source question turns on and because a reference collection in a national antiquities department is exactly the kind of thing a comparative database should contain and may not. Every carnelian bead in the Gulf attributed to India on the assumption that no local source existed was attributed under a premise that has since failed.
